title: Base32 uses 5-bit grouping and specific alphabetical order
summary: Standard Base32 values 0 to 25 are A to Z, and 26 to 31 are 2 to 7.
applies: Binary encoding; file and value dumps
detail: Base32hex is arranged from 0 to 9, A to V. There are overlapping characters in the two alphabets but their numerical values may be different.
boundary: Just because the characters appear in both alphabets, it cannot be judged that the decoding results are consistent.
relevance: Clarify which Base32 variant to use when the charset appears to be normal but the output bytes are wrong.
